newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt approves delay to oil reserve deadline.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt approves delay to oil reserve deadline.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday gave the go-ahead to a proposal to delay the deadline for doubling imported gas oil and fuel oil reserves to 1999 from 1997, a government official said.
Reserves on imported refined products other than fuel oil and gas oil will be increased to 10 percent from five percent now by January 1997 as previously scheduled, she said.
The proposal was made by the board of National Energy Policy Office (NEPO) in October.
The decision to push back the rise on gas and fuel oil was made after a request from the commerce ministry, which said the increases could affect industry and lead to higher inflation.

The move to double oil reserves on imported refined product was to ensure sufficient reserves and to reduce the advantage importers have over local producers who are currently required to reserve five percent of their crude imports and five percent of oil products.
During the first nine months of 1996, Thailand's consumption of refined products reached an average 726,550 barrels per day or a 10.4 percent rise from the same period last year.
